title: Claimed event omitted when _safePay reverts now unreachable, but emission gate in stake/unstake/claim is inconsistent with rewardDebt advancement
description:
Previously, `_safePay` returned the paid amount (possibly less than requested) and the Claimed event was gated on `paid > 0` while `rewardDebt` advanced to the full accrual. Story-002's fix makes `_safePay` revert on shortfall, which means the paid amount always equals the requested `pending` (when `pending > 0`). So the old 'silent forfeiture with no event' concern is resolved — any shortfall now reverts the whole transaction.

However, the code still has some residual inconsistency worth cleaning up:
1. `claim()` at line 284-289: uses variable name `paid`; emits only if `paid > 0`; unconditionally advances `rewardDebt` at line 289 even when `pending == 0` (line 289 runs regardless).
2. `stake()` at line 251-256 and `unstake()` at line 269-273: reassign `pending = _safePay(pending)`, emit only if `pending > 0`, advance `rewardDebt` at lines 260 and 276.

Now that `_safePay` reverts on shortfall, the reassignment of `pending = _safePay(pending)` in stake/unstake is a no-op (it's just `pending = pending`). The code reads as if the return value might differ, which obscures the post-fix semantics. The variable naming between `paid` (in claim) and `pending` (in stake/unstake) is also inconsistent for no reason.

Separately: when `pending == 0` in `claim()`, the function still runs `_syncBudget` and unconditionally advances `user.rewardDebt`. For a user with zero stake this is a no-op; for a user whose rewardDebt was already current (no accrual since last action), it's also a no-op. But the `_syncBudget` side-effects still run, which is the grief vector discussed in CS-01 of this report.
impact: Code-quality / clarity. No direct value at risk. The dead-code-on-success pattern (`pending = _safePay(pending)` where the return always equals input) misleads reviewers about the function's semantics and could mask a future regression if `_safePay` is changed to return less than requested again.
proof: Read lines 253-254, 271-272, 286-287 together. `_safePay` now either (a) reverts on balance shortfall, or (b) returns `amount` unchanged. The return-value reassignment in each call site is dead on success. The inconsistency with `claim`'s `paid` variable vs `stake`/`unstake`'s `pending` reassignment is purely stylistic.
suggested-fix: Either: (a) remove the return value from `_safePay` entirely — make it return void or just a bool — and stop reassigning `pending`/`paid` after the call; or (b) commit to the rollover design and have `_safePay` return a possibly-reduced paid amount, with call sites using that to compute rolled-over debt. Pick one and document the intent. Rename local variables to match (both sites use `paid`, not `pending`). Add an assertion `assert(paid == pending)` in the success path to make the invariant explicit.
